correctness.rationale: For n≥3 over an arbitrary characteristic-two field the product is (I+S)(x∘y) with constant kernel. The original defining equations split exhaustively into a nonzero cross-product branch (three-column Frobenius argument forces all images a·w) and a disjoint-support branch (each image a coordinate vector; multiplication forces a cyclic rotation with coefficient 1). The two families satisfy the original identities. Their ranks, composition table, ideal lattice, and parity of the square-zero complement follow by direct calculations. Exact direct exhaustive independent-identity checks of 512+65536+262144 linear maps match the formulas, but the general proof does not rely on them. No statement is made for n=2 or odd characteristic.

value.rationale: The exact unrestricted endomorphism monoid of an all-dimensional, naturally Cayley-defined, strongly connected but nonperfect evolution algebra is a motivated structural invariant. It has a sharp intermediate-rank gap, an exact finite-field rank polynomial, a new parity-dependent composition law and a nontrivial criterion for splitting its unique codimension-one square ideal. These genuinely distinguish the singular cyclic family from perfect cycles and nilpotent chains and do not reduce to an arbitrary small example.
